ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a circle, points A and C are at the left and right ends of the circle, and line segment AC horizontally passes through the circle center O, so AC is a diameter, and O is the midpoint of AC. Point B is above the circle, and AB, BC, and BO are connected. The gray shaded region is triangle AOB. Reasoning: Because A and C are the two endpoints of diameter AC, and O is the circle center, AO = OC. Triangle ABC is divided by line segment BO into two triangles AOB and BOC. Their bases are AO and OC respectively, and both use the perpendicular distance from B to line AC as the height. Since the bases are equal and the heights are the same, area(AOB) = area(BOC). It is known that the shaded area area(AOB) = sqrt(3), therefore area(ABC) = area(AOB) + area(BOC) = sqrt(3) + sqrt(3) = 2sqrt(3).

method.method_draft: Identify from the image that A and C are endpoints of a diameter passing through O, so O is the midpoint of AC. The shaded region is triangle AOB, and triangle ABC is split by segment BO into triangles AOB and BOC.
